survey: An astronaut helmet sits on a pale shelf, turned about three-quarters to the left. Main parts: (1) The shell is a round white dome. Its bottom edge meets the neck ring. (2) The visor is a domed amber pane set into the front-left of the shell, inside an oval chrome rim. The rim follows the shell's curve. (3) The neck ring at the base has two parts: a thin chrome collar where the shell sits, and a wide white cylinder with a red band below it. The cylinder's flat bottom rests on the shelf, and a contact shadow shows beneath it, so the helmet is supported. The shell, collar and base line up on one axis. The visor has no hinge or pivot, but that counts as a simplification. There are no cables, straps or invented parts.

errors.where: Chrome visor rim, right side (about 3 o'clock on the oval, where it meets the shell)
errors.what: The rim tube is not a continuous ring. It has a visible cut where the two ends meet slightly out of line, as if the loop was never closed. A real visor seal is one unbroken ring, or it shows a clear hinge or clamp at that point.

fix: Make the chrome rim around the amber visor one smooth, continuous ring with no seam, break or offset on its right side, evenly thick all the way around.
